title: Introduce KMS Attestor proxy and residency-aware audit TTL manager
author: Priya Nambiar
body: Summary: Adds a lightweight KMS attestor proxy service and a residency-aware audit TTL manager. The attestor verifies signed KMS residency assertions (from supported CMK providers), enforces policy-based routing and RBAC checks, and annotates requests with a signed residency-attestation header. The audit TTL manager consumes residency assertions and per-tenant policy to attach audit retention TTLs and retention-flag headers that downstream logging/audit systems use to enforce region-specific retention/scrubbing requirements. Motivation: Customers with stringent data residency rules require cryptographically verifiable proof of where keys are domiciled and that logs tied to requests will be retained only as allowed by region. This PR closes gaps identified in SUP-9482 and ENG-1209: previously we had a best-effort KMS-region tag and an SLO-driven audit sampler, but no authenticated assertion path and no enforcement point to attach retention policies pre-ingestion. Changes in this PR: - New service: kms-attestor (Go) - verifies KMS-signed residency assertions and caches verification results with a TTL - Residency assertion format v1 spec (JSON, JWS-signed) and validation logic - Residency policy engine (YAML) mapping tenant -> allowed regions -> max-retention-days - Audit TTL manager (nodejs small binary) that maps assertion+policy -> X-Audit-Retention and X-Audit-Region headers and signs an envelope header for audit systems - RBAC v2 integration: attestor consults rbac-decision API for cross-region access checks (deny if tenant policy forbids) - Fallback mode: when attestation absent, fallback to best-effort region inference and mark request with X-Attestation-Status: unknown; strict mode denies requests without attestation - Integration points: API gateway middleware, dedicated private deployment hooks, and observability (span attributes and metrics) - Tests: unit + integration tests that exercise signer verification, policy enforcement, and TTL mapping - Documentation: design doc, operator runbook, sample tenant policy and migration notes Design notes: - Attestation verification supports AWS KMS and GCP KMS assertion formats (adapter pattern) and will be extensible to other providers. - Verification caching keyed by attestation token hash with a TTL of 10m by default to avoid repeated signature checks for high-throughput customers. - Audit TTL derivation: tenant policy defines retention bounds per region and per data-class. The manager resolves most conservative retention consistent with policy and attaches explicit TTL in seconds along with a signed envelope so downstream sinks can validate source of TTL. - RBAC policy enforcement is executed before any audit headers are emitted. If RBAC denies access to a region, the request is rejected with 403 and a structured error explaining required attestation claims. - Migration strategy: roll out in three phases: 1) opt-in mode (attestations accepted and headers emitted but not enforced), 2) enforcement for new tenants with strict mode on, 3) global enforcement (legacy fallback disabled) Rollout & compatibility: - Default deployment will be opt-in via feature flag feature.kms_attestor.opt_in - Public hosted customers are not impacted until feature toggled or tenant policy bound - Private/Dedicated customers can enable strict mode via config - Backward compatibility: when older clients do not send attestation headers, behavior depends on tenant policy (opt-in -> allowed; strict -> denied) Security considerations: - All attestation validation code runs in a hardened process with restricted network egress - Signed headers use our internal signing key (rotated by KMS) and include nonce+timestamp to prevent replay - Cache entries respect attestation expiry to avoid stale routing decisions Testing: - Unit tests for parser/validator, adapters for AWS/GCP - End-to-end integration test spin up kms-attestor, a mock-KMS attestor provider, and the audit-ttl-manager to validate mappings - Performance test: ensured attestor proxy adds <2ms median per-request overhead with 99th percentile <5ms when verification cache hits - CI integrates with existing e2e matrix and added a new job security/kms-attestor that runs the verification matrix Commits (high level): - feat(kms-attestor): add verification service and adapters - feat(audit-ttl): add audit TTL manager and envelope signer - feat(rbac): hook rbac-decision checks into attestor flow - docs: design + runbook + tenant policy examples - test: add unit and integration tests - ci: add security/kms-attestor job Changed files (high level): - internal/kms/attestor/{main.go, verifier.go, adapters_aws.go, adapters_gcp.go, cache.go, policy.go} - services/audit-ttl-manager/{index.js, policy-resolver.js, signer.js} - docs/security/kms-attestor.md - docs/operator/runbooks/kms-attestor-runbook.md - infra/helm/kms-attestor.yaml - api/gateway/middleware/attestation_middleware.go - tests/integration/kms_attestor_e2e_test.go - examples/policies/sample-residency-policy.yaml Review conversation (high level timeline): - 2026-02-22 Owen Carter: initial review asking for clarification on cache invalidation window and replay protections. - 2026-02-23 Priya Nambiar: response added nonce+timestamp to signed header and lowered default cache TTL to 10m; pushed commit feat(kms-attestor): tighten cache invalidation and add nonce. - 2026-02-25 Marta Ruiz: requested a clearer operator rollback path and a migration checklist; author added runbook and migration steps. - 2026-02-27 Amit Shah: asked for explicit tests for RBAC deny path; author added integration tests and a failing-case unit test. - 2026-02-28 CI flake on security/kms-attestor job due to ephemeral mock KMS network timeouts; rerun fixed. - 2026-03-01 Reviews approved by Owen Carter and Marta Ruiz. Merge: squash and merge. Post-merge actions: - Create Linear tasks to instrument long-tail metrics for attestation failures ENG-1225 - Add a scheduled job to reconcile cached attestation rejections with KMS provider revocations ENG-1231 - Product outreach: post an announcement to affected tenants about opt-in window. CI summary: - security/kms-attestor: pass - unit: pass - integration: pass (mock KMS) - lint: pass - e2e: pass with synthetic tenant policies Migration notes for operators: - Default behavior is opt-in. To enable strict enforcement in a deployment, set config: KMS_ATTESTOR_STRICT=true and provide policy bundle path. - If enabling strict mode, run the migration plan: 1) enable opt-in and monitor attach_rate and attestation_failure_rate 2) contact tenants with high failure_rate for onboarding 3) flip strict mode for tenant subsets 4) when stable, flip global enforcement - To rollback: disable KMS_ATTESTOR_STRICT and clear any feature flags; the attestor can be toggled off in the helm chart Known limitations: - Initial provider adapters limited to AWS/GCP KMS assertion formats only - Attestation v1 does not yet support multi-cmk aggregated statements (planned v2) - Audit sinks must be updated to validate envelope signature to fully trust TTL headers Release notes (short): Adds KMS attestor proxy and residency-aware audit TTL manager. Enables cryptographically verifiable KMS residency assertions and per-tenant retention header emission. Opt-in by default; strict enforcement gated behind feature flag and tenant policy. Related: SUP-9482, ENG-1209, ENG-1217.
